description.value: The Thunderbird Café occupies the admission-free lower level of the Squamish Lil'wat Cultural Centre in Whistler's Upper Village, serving Indigenous-inspired dishes such as bannock tacos, venison chili, and cedar plank salmon chowder prepared with fresh local ingredients. Staffed by Cultural Ambassadors of the Squamish and Lil'wat Nations, the café offers a culturally grounded dining experience that stands apart from Whistler's typical resort fare. Free Wi-Fi and a comfortable seating environment make it a practical rest stop for cyclists before or after exploring the museum exhibits.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: Website content from slcc.ca/thunderbird-cafe/ is fully available and confirms an active, publicly accessible café at 4584 Blackcomb Way inside the Squamish Lil'wat Cultural Centre. Wi-Fi is explicitly confirmed by the phrase 'The Thunderbird Café also offers free wireless internet.' No bike parking, water refill, washroom access, or takeout details appear anywhere in the website text, so those fields remain null; OSM provides no supplementary tags for these either.
concerns: OSM name is 'Thunderbird Cafe' (no accent); website consistently uses 'Thunderbird Café' (with accent on the e).

Café-specific phone +1 604 972 1085 (shown on the café page with 'Call the Cafe' link) differs from the general SLCC toll-free number 1-866-441-7522 on the contact page; the café-direct number is used here.
No bike parking information found in website content or OSM tags; this required criterion cannot be confirmed.
OSM had no phone or address tags, so contact_confirmed reflects only the website URL match.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: Active, publicly accessible café inside a prominent Whistler cultural centre with distinctive Indigenous-inspired cuisine and confirmed free Wi-Fi; a worthwhile and culturally notable stop for touring cyclists.
